pr.title: Write the iOS rules into AGENTS.md only for a repository with an iOS app
pr.head: 3932031b94be909cf5582dabcf7bf2787d7f4957

summary: project init writes a marked section, the Projector section, into every adopting repository's AGENTS.md, and Claude Code reads it through CLAUDE.md. project check warns when the committed section differs from the template the CLI ships. The template's version number is in its begin marker, so a section with the template's version but different text reads as a hand edit.

Version 28 added two paragraphs about building an iOS app with project ios. Every repository got them, including the many with no app. This pull request keeps those paragraphs only where an iOS app exists:

1. The template marks the paragraphs. agents-block.md, now version 29, wraps them in {ios} and {/ios} lines. instructions.render keeps them, or drops them with the blank line after each.
  2. The store decides which rendering a repository gets. ProjectStore._carries_ios_rules asks Git for each *.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj that is tracked, or untracked and not ignored, and counts one only when it names the iOS SDK, iphoneos. A configured ios.project forces the rules on. The new boolean instructions.ios overrides both.
  3. check tells the renderings apart. A same-version section that matches the other rendering gets the new warning instructions-ios instead of instructions-edited, and init rewrites it.

This repository has no Xcode project, so its own AGENTS.md drops the two paragraphs. The first review found two problems, and the second head fixes both. A Mac-only Xcode project no longer counts as an iOS app, because project ios builds only for iOS. The module docstring of instructions.py now describes both renderings. The review of 3932031 is clean.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Projector section: the block between <!-- projector:begin N --> and <!-- projector:end --> that init owns.
  • Rendering: the section's text for one repository, with or without the iOS paragraphs.
  • Pin: the SHA-256 of the template that tests/test_instructions.py records per version, so a text change without a version bump fails the suite.

groups.title: The template marks the iOS paragraphs
groups.kicker: Version 29 of the section, and how render keeps or drops its iOS part
intro: The template is the one source for every repository's Projector section. It now marks the two iOS paragraphs so that render can leave them out. Because the paragraphs now appear only where an app exists, the first opens with "This repository has an iOS app" in place of "In a repository with an iOS app".
The version moves from 28 to 29 and gets a new pin. The pin hashes the template, not a rendering, so one pin per version covers both renderings.

files.note: The template: the version bump, the {ios} and {/ios} lines around both paragraphs, and the new opening sentence.

checks.text: This sentence now states as fact that the repository has an iOS app. The detection in core.py decides when it appears, so a false positive there makes this sentence false.

files.note: IOS_SECTION matches each marked paragraph run and its following blank line. render gains an ios flag, false by default.

checks.text: The module docstring now says that one template version renders two ways, and that a same-version block matching the other rendering belongs to a repository that gained or lost its app.

files.note: Pins version 29 and checks that both renderings drop the markers and keep the paragraphs around the iOS part one blank line apart.

groups.title: The store chooses a rendering and check tells them apart
groups.kicker: Detection, the configuration that overrides it, and the new warning
intro: ProjectStore now holds an optional ios answer. When configuration gives none, _carries_ios_rules runs git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard for *.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj, once per command, and caches the result. A project counts only when its file names iphoneos as a whole word, as SDKROOT = iphoneos or a multiplatform target's SUPPORTED_PLATFORMS does. project ios builds only for iOS, so a Mac-only project gets no rules. A new iOS project counts before its first commit, and a dependency's project in an ignored folder does not.

_block_issues compares the section with the detected rendering first, then with the other one. Only a section that matches neither is instructions-edited. init writes the detected rendering, so it adds or removes the rules when an app arrives or leaves.

checks.text: project ios finds its project differently. ios.find_project walks a fresh worktree at a commit, skips Pods, node_modules, build, and .build, and needs exactly one project or workspace. The section's detection also counts untracked files and drops only ignored ones. A workspace counts only through the projects it holds.

files.note: The detection in _carries_ios_rules and _builds_for_ios, and the second comparison in _block_issues that gives instructions-ios.

checks.text: Checked in temporary repositories at this head. A macosx project and a watchOS project that mentions only IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET get no rules. A multiplatform target that lists iphoneos gets them, and so does an iOS project beside a workspace. A tracked project.pbxproj that is missing from the working tree gets none, and neither does an unreadable one.
In this repository, the committed AGENTS.md matches render("docs/projects") and not render("docs/projects", ios=True), and project check prints no warning. Checked by running both at the head.

files.note: instructions_ios reads instructions.ios, falls back to true when ios.project is set, and is passed to the store in run. The digest that upgrade compares renders the iOS variant, so a change to either part of the template changes it.

End-to-end check and init runs in temporary repositories: an untracked, then tracked, then removed iOS project, an ignored project, Mac-only, simulator-only, and workspace-only repositories that get no rules, a multiplatform target that does, and the two settings overriding detection.
